thought.text: The memory spike has subsided (currently 2.6GB in use). The two stuck processes are hung bash/uv wrappers (11–16MB each, child processes already terminated). I'll force-kill these and restart all four affected services:

reasoning_content:
Interesting point: the process that matched "18021|18022" is a bash wrapper (uv run), at about 11-16MB each, with elapsed time 1595 seconds (about 27 minutes) — these are the original processes from run 1! They've been left over as bash/uv wrappers without child processes (the child uvicorn has terminated). And total app memory is only 2.6GB right now — the memory spike has subsided.

Wait, elapsed time 1595 seconds = 27 minutes — that's the original instance from run 1 (23:45 + 27 min ≈ 00:12). These are zombie wrapper processes from the run 1 process-compose... hmm, actually process-compose should have cleaned them up when it stopped. Or did these wrappers belong to run 2? Run 2 started at 23:45, and now it's about 00:12, so 1595 seconds ≈ 26.5 minutes — matches run 2's start time.

Wait, but these are "18021"/"18022" — jura-db and begruendungen. Are they the current ones (the "Terminating" ones) or leftovers? Elapsed time 27 minutes means they've been running continuously since the run 2 start (23:45). The "Terminating" state began a few minutes ago. So these are the run 2 jura-db/begruendungen processes stuck in graceful shutdown — but the memory usage is only 11-16MB (bash/uv wrapper level). Their uvicorn children have already terminated, and the wrappers are hung waiting for the children.

Hmm wait, total app memory is currently 2607MB — low. The spike (6.8–7.1GB) has passed. Good.

Let's force-kill the hung wrappers, and restart these two and objections/codec via the API.

Actually — I should check: are 65820/65822/65838/65846 the uv run wrappers for jura-db (18021) and begruendungen (18022)? If so, their uvicorn children have already terminated (killed). The wrappers are hung waiting. I'll force-kill them, then restart them via the process-compose API.

action.command:
cd /workspace
for p in 65820 65822 65838 65846; do kill -KILL $p 2>/dev/null && echo "killed $p"; done
sleep 5
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "jura-db -> %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:8080/process/start/jura-db
sleep 20
free -h | awk 'NR==2{print "mem now:", $3" used", $7" avail"}'
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "begruendungen -> %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:8080/process/start/gesetzesbegruendung-db
